name: Katmai National Park and Preserve
blurb: Brown bears, sockeye salmon and a landscape rebuilt after a volcano.

tip.title: Cut the salmon run
tip.text: Salmon feed bears, gulls, ravens and eagles and carry nutrients inland. Set Sockeye salmon to -100% and watch bears, scavengers and the nutrient flow.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Katmai National Park and Preserve

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Katmai National Park and Preserve, Brown bear, Sockeye salmon). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: The 1912 Novarupta eruption buried the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes under deep ash and pumice deposits, where plants are slowly recolonizing.
Fungi and bacteria break down salmon carcasses and other dead matter, returning nutrients to soil and water.
A low evergreen tundra shrub with black berries that birds eat.
A low berry shrub of tundra and bog. Its berries are eaten by bears.
A tall pink wildflower that quickly colonizes bare or disturbed ground and is browsed by moose.
Microscopic drifting algae that form the base of the food web in park lakes.
Browses shrubs, horsetail and other plants. Wikipedia lists moose among park mammals; bears and wolves hunt them.
A burrowing, hibernating rodent of tundra slopes that eats plants and seeds and is prey for bears.
Feeds on spruce seeds and is prey for lynx and bears.
A small rodent of wet meadows that feeds on sedges and other plants and is eaten by bears.
Feeds on zooplankton, then returns from the ocean to spawn. Spawning runs into Brooks River bring bears, eagles and gulls to feed.
A secretive wild cat listed among park mammals. It hunts squirrels and other small prey.
An opportunistic omnivore that eats berries and scavenges salmon remains and carrion.
Feeds on spawning salmon and on carcasses left on riverbanks.
Katmai protects one of the largest brown bear populations in the world. Bears eat sedges, berries, and in summer, salmon.
Listed among Katmai mammals. Wolves hunt large prey such as moose.

story: Katmai National Park and Preserve in southwest Alaska is known for the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes and for its brown bears. The park covers 4,093,077 acres and includes as many as 18 volcanoes, seven of them active since 1900. Most of it is designated wilderness.
matters: The 1912 Novarupta eruption formed the valley, a 40-square-mile pyroclastic flow up to 700 feet deep. The area became a national monument in 1918.
